                                           Message




Under the visionary leadership of the Hon’ble Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, the government
of Bangladesh continues to give education highest priority and has set up a number of
programmes and initiatives in this sector to achieve the desired level of development of the
country. Bangladesh is determined to ensure quality and global standard education in
harmony with the changes across the world. For achieving the SDG-4 targets by 2030, an
effective and efficient education planning and management is mandatory.

In order to transform the country from a developing to a developed country, it is necessary to
ensure the availability of accurate and timely statistics in every sector, particularly in
education. To serve this purpose, each year BANBEIS publishes ‘Bangladesh Education
Statistics’ presenting the latest education statistics status of the country with the support from
different organizations. The Bureau works closely with Ministry of Education to improve
quality of data as per nation’s demand.

I am happy to know that Bangladesh Bureau of Educational Information and Statistics
(BANBEIS) is going to publish ‘Bangladesh Education Statistics-2022’ after conducting a
successful Annual Education Survey-2022. The report has been prepared focusing on the
essential indicators and statistics in line with the eighth five-year plan perspectives and SDG-4.
It will provide a complete scenario of all levels of education of the country. I hope this report
will help in reviewing the country’s progress along with SDG-4. It will also be useful to
education planners, policy makers, development partners and researchers to prescribe policy
measures for achieving national and universal goals.

I would like to thank all the Heads of the Institutions and Organizations who provided data
and gave support in bringing out the report. I also take this opportunity to express my
heartfelt thanks and appreciation to all officials of BANBEIS for their relentless efforts to
complete this laborious job in the stipulated time.

Joy Bangla, Joy Bangabandhu,
May Bangladesh live forever.




(Dr. Dipu Moni, M.P.)

      Ministry of Education

                                          Message



Our Government is committed to collecting and publishing the necessary, timely and quality statistics
for decision-making and planning in all areas. The Government constantly strives for timely and
expeditious use of modern technology in data processing, identification, on-demand data supply and
statistical activities to make the right decisions to meet the challenges of globalization. I appreciate
the endeavours of BANBEIS for its contribution over the years.

BANBEIS conducts Online Education Survey every year that brings out the stoic data of our
education sector and prepares a comprehensive report outlining essential indicators in the field of
education. I am delighted to know that BANBEIS is going to publish a complete and resourceful
report titled “Education Statistics 2022”.

The present Government’s one of the primary aims is to realize the Vision 2041. I hope all working in
the education sector and related stakeholders will find this report valuable in getting accurate data for
policymaking to meet SDG-4 targets.

My sincere thanks to the concerned for their outstanding effort in completing the report in the
scheduled time. I congratulate the Director General of BANBEIS for his continued directions and
unflinching commitment to this publication.

Joy Bangla, Joy Bangabandhu,
May Bangladesh live forever.

                                              Message



Education aims to acquire the necessary skills and expected qualities to meet the basic needs of a
person's behavior. This resonates the necessity of world-class education, knowledge, science, skills
and technology in our education. Bangladesh is committed to ensuring quality and world-class
education aligned with global change.

Bangladesh has already elevated itself from a least developed country to a developing country. To
uphold the continued development efforts in a sustainable platform, all UN member states showed
their consent to adopt the Sustainable Development Goals 2030 (SDG) measure in September 2015.
The Government is working relentlessly to achieve the targets of SDG-4 by 2030.

Ensuring the availability of accurate and time-befitting education statistics is essential for achieving
the SDG-4 goals. For this purpose, BANBEIS publishes "Bangladesh Education Statistics" every
year, which presents the updated education data of the country. BANBEIS is working with relevant
stakeholders to improve the data quality according to the needs of the country.

I am happy to know that BANBEIS is going to publish the 'Bangladesh Education Statistics 2022'
report based on the education data collected through the online survey. The information in the report
will play an important role in formulating the Government's short and long-term policies, plans and
development strategies.

I hope this report will meet the needs of the stakeholders for the necessary and relevant information in
determining the strategy of the Five-Year Plan and the Annual Development Program. This report will
contribute to achieving the goals of Vision-2021 and SDG-2030.

My sincere thanks to all those involved in conducting the survey and publishing the report. I would
also like to express my sincere thanks to the Director General of BANBEIS, who led a tremendous
journey and successfully compiled the information repository within the stipulated time.

                                             Message




We all know that education is the first step towards the development of a nation, so, there is no
alternative but to invest in education sector to develop its human resources. Education plays a vital
role in social, cultural, economic and political fields of a country. The SDG-4 focuses on quality
education that contributes to building a sustainable society which is also very essential for achieving
other goals of the SDG-2030.

I affirm that the Government is determined to elevate Bangladesh into a developed and prosperous
country by 2041. The vision of the Government is only possible to translate into reality through
improvising advanced training and time-befitting development of technical and vocational education.

I am happy learn that the Bangladesh Bureau of Educational Information and Statistics (BANBEIS)
has completed the online Annual Education Survey 2022 and has prepared a detailed report and
statistics highlighting various indicators of education. This report will play an important role in the
planning and decision-making by policymakers on the expansion of quality technical and vocational
education.

In the recent past, enrolment in technical education has increased quite significantly, and a number of
new technical and vocational educational institutions have been established as part of the
government’s various initiatives. The Education Survey-2022 report has reflected that information
regarding the recent improvement in technical and vocational education. Therefore, the report will
foster a special role by creating a positive attitude among the people about technical and vocational
education, and ultimately this will further increase students’ participation in technical education.

My heartiest congratulations to all who have worked rigorously to conduct the survey and publish the
survey report on time.

Joy Bangla

                                                Preface



Bangladesh Bureau of Educational Information and Statistics (BANBEIS) has a long history of
conducting Education Surveys to track progress in educational statistics in Bangladesh. Established in
1976-1977 as a department attached to the Ministry of Education (MoE), BANBEIS has been
entrusted with the critical responsibility of collecting, consolidating, providing, and disseminating
educational data and statistics.
Education plays a crucial role in developing a nation's human resources. Under the visionary
leadership of Honorable Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, Bangladesh is striving to achieve the goals set
in the SDGs and implementing the Vision 2041 perspective plan to make the country developed and
prosperous.
Information, data, and evidence are important elements that help us understand the situation and make
effective decisions towards achieving our desired goals. "Bangladesh Education Statistics 2022" is an
annual report that provides a comprehensive presentation of education statistics at all levels in the last
year. The publication is prepared by collecting information through online surveys and various types
of data from primary and secondary educational institutions. Relevant educational institutions update
information online and upload it to the database server. Quality assurance (QA) is ensured in the field
of information collection. The database manages post-enumeration checks (PEC) regularly to ensure
data quality. The database also includes education-related information published by the Primary
Education Department of Bangladesh, which is incorporated into the Bangladesh Education Statistics
publication. Since education levels and fields are interrelated, all relevant education statistics must be
published in a single publication.

I express my gratitude to the officers and staff of BANBEIS who have contributed to preparing this
valuable report. I sincerely acknowledge the contribution of all the heads of institutions as survey
respondents. I would also like to thank all the field officers (DEO, USEO, AP), and others who have
provided their inputs to publish this report. Special thanks to BBS, DPE, and UGC for their
collaboration in preparing this comprehensive report concerning all levels of education.

Despite our best efforts to ensure a impeccable publication, there is a possibility that it may contain
minor errors and shortcomings. We value constructive criticism and welcome any pragmatic
suggestions and recommendations to enhance future publications. We assure that we will take
appropriate measures to incorporate your feedback and improve the quality of our work.




 BANBEIS                                                                     (Md. Muhibur Rahman)

                                     Definition of terms
Enrolment: Number of Students officially enrolled in a given grade or level of education regardless
of age.

Class size: The average number of students together in a class enrolled.

Teacher Student Ratio (TSR): Refers to the proportion of teachers in relation to the number of
students in an institution. Calculated by dividing the total number of students in a school or group of
school by the total number of teachers them.

Urban Area: Refers to the area covered by municipalities, Upa-zila Head Quarters, District Head
Quarters and City Corporations in the country.

Cohort Survival Rate: Percentage of students enrolled at the beginning grade/year of the level of
education who reached the final grade/year at the end of the required number of year to the level of
education.

Dropout Rate: Refers to the percentage of students of any reason leave educational institutions (in
any given grade or level) and did not come back to finish the grade or level during that school years of
that level of education.

Completion Rate: The percentage of pupils/students in the beginning grade/year of the level of
education who finished or graduated from the final grade/year at the required number of years of that
level of education.

Gross Enrolment Ratio: Refers to the total enrolment of students in a grade or level of
education, regardless of age, expressed as percentage of the corresponding eligible official
age- group population in a given school year.

Net Enrolment Rate: Refers to the number of students enrolled in the official specific age
group expressed as a percentage of the total population in that age group.

School age Population: Population of the age group theoretically corresponding to a given
level of education as indicated by theoretical entrance age and duration e.g the population
from ages four ages to thirty inclusive regardless of the existing requirements of compulsory
education or the period of education provided for in various types of schools.

Co-efficient of Efficiency: It is a ratio of expected student years’ student years required to
complete the cycle by the graduates and the total years actually spent to produce those
graduates expressed in percentage terms. The ideal (optimal) number of pupil-years required
(i.e.in the absence of repetition and dropout) to produce a number of graduates from a given
school-cohort for secondary education expressed as a percentage of the actual number of
pupil-years spent to produce the same number of graduates.

This is a synthetic indicator of the internal efficiency of an educational system. It summarises
the consequences of repetition and dropout on the efficiency of the educational process in
producing graduates.

School Expectancy: The number of years a person of School entrance age can expect to
spend within the specified level of education.

Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):


Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) are the universal commitment of the member states of United
Nations. To ensure peace and prosperities for the people of the planet by establishing partnership of all,
the 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) were designed to eradicate poverty and hunger by
ensuring protection of natural resources and climate for the future generation. Now the present context
of the world every country is surviving to achieve SDGs. Bangladesh is also committed to achieve
SDGs by inspiring its wonderful success in Millennium Development Goals


Education is the very much influential target of SDGs which is also the key instrument of development.
To ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities
for all, Goal 4 has been adopted aiming to attain 10 Global Targets. There are 12 Global Indicators as
well as 31 Thematic Indicators for the monitoring of quality education. Bangladesh has made
remarkable progress in improving access to education at all levels. It also gradually moving forward to
achieve the Sustainable Development Goal 4.

                                    Executive Summary


Introduction:
The education system of Bangladesh is comprised of mix of heterogeneous providers. A
variety of schools operate within the country; government run schools, privately run schools
and madrasah, English medium schools (British Curriculum), schools run by NGOs and
kindergarten schools. Primary education spans grade 1-5; Junior secondary grades 6-8,
secondary grade 9-10, higher secondary grade 11-12 and tertiary education grades 13 and
above. It is noted that the government is going to implement primary education comprising
from grade I-VIII.

Bangladesh has a centralized Education system administered by the Ministry of Education
(MOE) with two divisions viz, Secondary and Higher Education Division (SHED) & Technical
and Madrasah Education Division (TMED) and the Ministry of Primary and Mass Education
(MOPME). The MOPME and DPE are responsible for planning and management of primary,
mass and pre-primary education. The MOE, DSHE and DTE are responsible for post-primary
education. The MOE and UGC look after the overall management of tertiary education.

Education is the pivotal tool of the development of any country. Given this view the incumbent
government has been giving top most importance to the expansion of education. For the past
decade Bangladesh has been investing more to achieve the education Millennium Development
Goals (MDGs). Besides reducing poverty, Bangladesh has made spectacular success in improving
access to education. The gross enrolment ratio in primary education in 2021 has reached 105.72%
and net enrolment rate 97.42%. The gross enrolment ratio in secondary education in 2022 reached
76.10% while net enrolment rate 73.76%. Bangladesh has achieved gender parity for educational
access in both primary and secondary education (well in advance of their 2015 MDGs). Now
disparity in favor of girl’s student both primary and secondary level. The number of out of school
children has been continuously decreasing both in absolute and relative term. Bangladesh
education system is large, catering to over 40.34 million students (2021), involving many
stakeholders (for example there are 14 types of providers in primary education, 11 examination
broads at the secondary levels, about 93.62% secondary education institutions are privately
managed).

For the planning and development of the education sector, the ministries need a complete quality
database. With a view to up-dating the database, BANBEIS regularly conducts post-primary
education surveys. The base-line survey was conducted in 2008 after that the annual survey was
conducted in 2009, 2010, 2011, 2012, 2013, 2014 ,2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021 and
2022. The purpose of Bangladesh Education Survey is to provide up-dated educational information
and key performance indicators to the policy makers and other stakeholders. The scope of Annual
Survey 2022 was very broad. All the educational institutions imparting post-primary education
were covered.
The present report based on Educational Survey 2022 data do not fully address issues such as
management, governance, equity and non-teaching staff. The socio-demographic
characteristics of students and teachers were not considered. One limitation of the survey is the
difficulty in obtaining data from English medium schools, Medical Colleges and Universities.
The Annual Education Survey 2022 has used 10 type questionnaires, one for each types of
institution. The questionnaires were presented to the Stakeholders Consultation Workshop and
took feedback and incorporated it before finalization. The questionnaires were also pretested
before finalization.

Questionnaires were up-loaded to Website viz; www.banbeis.gov.bd to fill up and sent it to
BANBEIS server through On-line. The data collection started on 16 October 2022 and
continued up to 05 November 2022. Editing was done at the field (USEO office) and head
office to ensure quality of data. Besides, Post Enumeration Check (PEC) was done for School,
College and Madrasahs to minimize errors. It was found that the main survey data were
reliable and valid. According to the Annual Survey 2022, there were 42727 Post Primary
Educational institutions in the country. Among them 36805 are unique Institutions holding
EIIN, besides 5922 Institutions are attached to other Institution. This number was 42648 in the
year 2021.



Primary Education:
Annual Primary School Census (APSC) 2021 was conducted by The Directorate of Primary
Education (DPE) and the data shown in this report about primary education as secondary
sources.

Bangladesh primary education (Preprimary to Grade V) system is very large, catering to 20.09
million students in 2021 through 25 types of providers. Among them the government primary
schools alone covered 13.47 million (67.09%) students. The total number of girl students was
9953252 (49.54%). The GPI 0.98 i.e., parity exists. In 2021 total teachers (GPS only) were
359095 with female teachers were 64.41% of all teachers. Variation was observed between
types of primary education institutions (Table 2.3)

Pre-primary education enrolment (Table-2.2) was 3125090 among them 1571608 (50.29%)
were girls. Drop-out was prevalent in every grade, the rate was higher in grade-4 3.92 (Table
2.23)

Gross Intake Rate (GIR) and Net Intake Rate (NIR) was 107.30% and 96.18% respectively
(Table 2.13). A small difference was observed between boys and girls. Gross Enrolment Ratio
(GER) and Net Enrolment Rate (NER) in primary education have been increasing during the
past decades. GER was 107.7% in 2010 and reached 105.72% in 2021. GER of girls
(106.14%) was higher than that of boys. NER in primary education was 94.8% in 2010 and
increased to 97.42% in 2021(Table 2.14). The growth was spectacular and confirms continuous
increase of access of school age children to education.
Drop-out rates have been continuously decreasing from 39.80% in 2010 to 14.15% in
2021(Table 2.24). Survival rates have shown a continuous growth trend from boys 65.90% and
girls 68.60% in 2010 to boys 85.25% and girls 87.1% in 2021(Table 2.25).

As a result of increasing the growth of access, retention and survival of students the primary
education coefficient of efficiency rate has been increasing from 62.30% in 2010 and rose to
85.35% in 2021(Table 2.26).


Junior, Secondary and Higher Secondary School Education:
Total institutions offering Junior and Secondary education were 21003 in 2022 including 650
upgraded government primary schools having student from grade VI to VIII. The number of
institutions in this sub-sector was 12012 in 1995, has been smoothly increasing. Side by Side
the enrolment and teachers also increased. In 2022, the total enrolment was 10.13 million
among them 5.54 million (54.69%) were girls giving gender parity index near 1.21. The
number of students per institution was 482 in 2022. Total teachers were 278608 with 85435
female teachers. The percentage of female teachers was 30.66 % in 2022 and 20.28 % in 2005.
In 2022, the teacher-student ratio (TSR) was 1:36 and the average number of teachers per
institution was only 13. Among all teachers 67.91% were trained. This percentage was 26.48%
in Junior Schools 71.31% in Secondary School and 73.37% in School & College (Table-3.4.4).

In the total institution in 2022 the share of Junior Secondary institutions was 11.28%,
Secondary institutions 78.74%, School and Colleges 6.88% and Upgraded Govt. Primary
Schools 3.09%. Among all institutions 21003, 93.62% were privately managed, only 3.29%
was publicly managed and upgraded govt. Primary was 3.09% (Table-3.1.2). Rural-Urban
distribution reveals that in 2022, 76.11% of institutions were located in rural areas, 67.12% of
teachers were working in the rural institutions, and 69.72 % student was studying in the rural
institution (Table 3.1.6).

The distribution by division reveals unequal distribution. As regards the number of institutions,
Sylhet had only 5.28% while Dhaka had 19.03 % of all institutions. As regards teacher the
share of Sylhet was 8.11% while Dhaka had 23.73%. As regards the enrolment, the share of
Sylhet was 6.20% while Dhaka had 23.46% (Table 3.1.5).

The Annual Education Survey 2022 reveals that 98.45% of all institutions had electricity
facility; the percentage was 90.29% in junior Secondary Schools, 99.49% in Secondary
Schools and 99.86% in School & College (Table-3.5.1). The number of institutions having
multimedia was 78.39%. This percentage was 24.53% in Junior Schools, 84.69% in Secondary
and 94.61% in School & College (Table-3.5.2). Relatively more institutions have computer
facility; 48.42% of junior secondary, 93.05% of secondary, 99.24% of School & College,
88.30% of all institutions (Table-3.5.3).

It is reported that 72.28% of all institutions have computer teacher though Computer education
is Compulsory for Secondary education. This percentage was 39.72% for Junior Schools,
75.17% for secondary schools and 92.60% for School & College (Table 3.5.4). It is found that
83.12% of institutions had internet facilities in 2022. It is also found that most of the
institutions have safe drinking water facilities 98.01% and about 97.33% institution have
separate toilet for girls’ students (Table 3.5.6, 3.5.7 & 3.5.8).



College Education:
The institutions offering post higher secondary education are included in college education.
The following types are recognized as Intermediate Colleges, Degree (Pass) Colleges, Degree
(Honors) Colleges and Master’s Colleges. The total institution involved in college education
has been increasing. The number was 3324 in 2010, 3475 in 2011, 3547 in 2012, 3793 in 2013,
3985 in 2014, 4113 in 2015, 4238 in 2016, 4419 in 2017, 4495 in 2018, 4551 in 2019, 4699 in
2020, 4729 in 2021 and 4747 in 2022. Majority (85.23%) of college was privately managed
and only 14.77% was government managed (Table 4.1.1).

There are three types of colleges; one is co-education and one is exclusively for girls and the
other is exclusively for boys. In 2022, there were 770 colleges (16.22%) exclusively for girls.
The sharing of college by education type as, intermediate college (School & College and
Higher Secondary College) was 2806 (59.11%), Degree (Pass) College 1048 (22.07%) and the
remaining 893 (18.81%) were Degree (Honors) College and Master’s College. The total
enrolment in 2022 was 4.832 million. Among them 2.429 million (50.27%) were girls. The
gender parity index was 1.01 (Girls to Boys). The share of intermediate colleges in total
enrolment was 18.03%, degree (pass) college 17.90%, degree (honors) college 29.32% and
master’s college 34.74% (Table 4.1.4). In 2022, a college had on an average 1018 students, the
highest average number of students was 8477 in master’s colleges and the lowest average
number of students was 310 in intermediate colleges (Table 4.1.6).

Total teachers in 4747 colleges were 143007. Among them 38604 (26.99%) were female and
there were small variations among all types of colleges (Table 4.1.6). The teacher-student ratio
was 1:34, highest in master’s colleges (1:105) and the lowest in higher secondary colleges
(1:16) (Table 4.1.5).

The number of colleges, teachers and students was found to vary across divisions. The highest
percentage of college was in Dhaka division 1060 (22.32%) followed by Rajshahi division 778
(16.38%) and lowest in the Sylhet division 296 (6.23%) (Table 4.1.8). At the same time, the
highest number of students was in Dhaka division 1313580 (27.18%) followed by Chattogram
division 861661 (17.83%) and the lowest was in Barishal division 304178 (6.29%) (Table
4.1.8). Rural and urban distributions reveal greater inequality. In overall distribution of
students’ population, 73.60% live in urban areas and 26.40% live in rural areas. Education
survey 2022 reveals that 53.78% of institutions are located in rural areas (Table 4.1.12).

Among all institutions 99.96 % had electricity, 90.37% had multimedia facility (Table 4.5.1),
88.25% had internet connectively (Table 4.5.3) and 41.18% had solar panel (Table 4.5.2).
Madrasah Education:
Madrasah education is a subsector of education sector of Bangladesh. This subsector is also
large, catering to over 4.02 million students including Ebtedayee. This is popularly known as
religious stream quite distinct from general stream. The total institutions offering post-primary
madrasah education was 7820 in 2002, rose to 9268 in 2022. Ebtedayee madrasah offers
primary equivalent while post-primary madrasah covers Dakhil, Alim, Fazil and Kamil; which
are equivalent to Secondary, Higher Secondary, Degree and Masters Education of general
stream.

In 2022 a total of 9268 madrasah offered Dakhil to Kamil education. Madrasahs are absolutely
privately managed. Dakhil, Alim and Fazil are privately managed. Out of 262 Kamil madrasah
only 3 were Government managed madrasahs. Among 9268 madrasahs 9265 (99.97%) were
privately managed. Among 9268 madrasahs 70.36% were Dakhil, 15.06% were Alim, 11.75%
were Fazil and 2.83% were Kamil. In 6521 Dakhil Madrasahs total students were 1412562;
more than 58.52% were girls. Average students per institution are 217. Total teachers were
119008 and Total Student were 2762277; The average teachers and students per institution
were 13 and 298. Teacher-student ratio was 1:23.

There were 1396 Alim Madrasah with 486127 students and 22407 teachers. Girl’s students and
Female teachers were 54.55% and 18.92% respectively. Average students per institution were
348 and average teacher per institution is 16 persons. Teacher student ratio was 1:22. In 2022
total Fazil madrasah was 1089 with 562670 students and 20901 teachers, girls’ students were
50.50% Female teachers were 19.43%. Average student per institution was 517 and average
teacher was 19 giving teacher-student ratios 1:27. There were 262 Kamil madrasah in 2022
with 300918 students and 6400 teachers. Girls student were 33.90% of total enrolment. Female
teachers were 22.05 % of total. Average students per institution was 1149 and average teachers
were 24, yielding teacher-student ratio of 1:47 (Table 5.1.7).

The distribution of madrasahs by division reveals that 13.08% madrasahs were located in
Dhaka, 17.78% in Chattogram, 16.18% in Rajshahi, 15.29% in Rangpur, 12.66% in Khulna,
12.54% in Barishal, 4.32% in Sylhet and 8.16% in Mymenshingh (Table: 5.2.5). Rural-Urban
distribution shows that 85.93% of all madrasahs were located in rural areas. Variation between
types of madrasahs and the rural share was as follows: Dhakil 89.74%, Alim 82.88%, Fazil
78.42%, Kamil 38.55% (Table: 5.2.6). Most of the madrasahs 95.89% prepare annual
development plan, 93.85% conduct co-curriculum activities. About 67.12% madrasahs use
computer for academic/pedagogy purposes. Only 36.04% madrasahs have science laboratories
and 12.75% madrasahs have Ramp for special needs student. About 5.89% and 4.58%
madrasah have introduced digital attendance for teacher and student respectively (Table:
5.5.4).

Among all teachers only 26.86% teachers were trained. This percentage varies between
21.79% in Kamil and 28.55% in Dakhil. Percentage of female trained teacher is 30.01% (Table
5.4.7).

between types of madrasahs was observed (Table 5.4.8).



Professional Education:
Professional Education includes 13 types of institutions. These are Medical University,
Medical College, Armed Forces & Army Medical College, Dental College & Dental Unit,
Nursing and Midwifery College & Institution, Homeopathic College, Unani/Ayurvedic,
Textile Technology, Leather Technology, Law College, Art College, Agriculture College, and
Library Science in 2022, there were 826 professional institutions in the country. This subsector
has been growing. In 2000 total institutions were only 187. This number increased to 826 in
2022 (Table:6.1).

Among 826 institutions 15.62% were public and 84.38% were private. The rate of growth has
seen higher in private professional institutions. The total students in 13 types of institutions
were 174888 in 2022 and 51789 in 2003, showing a continuous growth in the past. Among all
students 61.49% were girls in 2022. The gender parity index was 1.60. The number of students
per institution was 212 in 2022, this number was 267 in public and 202 in private institutions.
Among all students, the percentage of students in medical college was 28.93%, 4.11% in
Dental College 26.21% in Homeopathic College, 4.25% in Law college, 24.25% in Nursing
College and 12.25% in other 8 types of institutions.

In 2022, there were 17409 teachers. Among them, 7634 (43.85%) were female teachers. GPI
was significantly improved and stands on 0.78, the teacher-student ratio was 1:10. The
percentage of female teachers was different in different type of institution, lowest (13.64%) in
Leather Technology and highest (77.46%) in Nursing and Midwifery college. Division wise
distribution shows that 36.20% institutions were in Dhaka, 14.53% in Rajshahi, 12.35% in
Chattogram, 10.17% in Khulna, 9.56% in Rangpur, 4.84% in Sylhet, 6.05% in Mymensingh
and 6.30% in Barishal.

Seven types of educational institutions comprise this sub-sector. These are: PTIs, TTC, TTTC,
VTTI Physical Education College, HSTTI and Bangladesh Madrasahs Teacher Training
Institute (BMTTI). This sector has been growing slowly. The total number of institutions was
129 in 2000, 143 in 2003, 215 in 2015,209 in 2021and 209 in 2022.

Among 209 institutions, 44.98% were government and 55.02% were privately managed. The
percentage by type of institution was: 49.76% was TTC, 32.02% PTIs 14.35% was Physical
Education College, and 3.83% were other institutions. About 23.44% were located in Dhaka
Division, 16.75% in Chittagong, 17.22% in Khulna, 15.31% in Rajshahi,9.09% in Rangpur,
3.83% in Sylhet,5.26% in Mymensingh and 9.09% in Barishal Division. This confirms uneven
distribution between divisions. There were only one TTTC, one VTTI and one MTTI in Dhaka
Division in the country.
Total trainee/students in 209 institutions were 33998 with an average of 163 per institution.

1990 was 32% (30% girls), increased to 88.10% (88.42% girls) in 2022 (Table 10.7). The pass
percentage in science group was 43.63% in 1990 and increased to 97.09% in 2022 (Table
10.8).

Pass rate in Vocational Examination (SSC) has seen a steady increase. The percentage of pass
was 68% in 1999 which increased to 89.55% in 2022. The Examination Result of Girl’s is
higher than that of boys, pass rate of girls was 76.35% in 2018, 77.47% in 2020 which is
91.80% in 2022 (Table 10.10). The pass rate in HSC has steadily increased. The pass rate in
1990 was 30% (31% girls) which has increased to 64.55%, (68.18% girls) in 2018. And due to
the COVID-19 Pandemic in 2020 HSC and equivalent Candidates were evaluated based on
their previous public examination results and all HSC candidates passed, Total number of
969338 students appeared in HSC in 2022 out of which 817230 students passed (427231 girls),
The overall pass rate is 84.31% (girls 86.34%) (Table 10.11). A total of 260132 students
appeared in the Madrasa Education Examination in 2022. The pass rate in Dakhil examination
is 82.22%, a total of 90266 students participated in Alim examination, the pass rate in Alim
examination is 92.56% (Table 10.15). The results of Fazil and Kamil tests are shown in (Table
10.17) and (Table 10.18) respectively.

SSC and Dakhil graduation results with grade points have also improved. A total of 8597 got
GPA 5 (A+) in SSC in 2004, 102845 in 2018, 123131 in 2020 and 233763 in 2022 (Table
10.19). Similarly, the submission GPA 5 score was 1288 in 2004, 3371 in 2018, 7516 in 2020
and 15457 in 2022 (Table 10.21). A similar trend is seen in SSC (Vocational) (Table 10.22),
H.S.C (Table 10.23) and Alim (Table 10.25). The Results of Degree (pass), Degree (Honours),
Masters and Equivalent Examinations under Public Universities are shown in (Table 10.27).
Compared to 2020, the total number of students has decreased slightly but the pass rate has
increased. The pass rate for Degree (pass), Degree (Honours), Masters and Equivalent
Examinations under Public Universities was 72% in 2020 and increased to 74% in 2021.

level. In 2022, the gender parity index (SDG indicator 4.5.1) for secondary level (6-10), higher
secondary level (11-12) and tertiary level were 1.21, 1.01 and 0.82 respectively; this was also
significantly increased and showing the high enrolment rate of girls in education against the

really remarkable but only 19.04 percentage of schools having the Ramp facility and 91.03
percent of schools having the basic hand washing facilities and 53.32 percent schools use the
Internet for pedagogical purposes though 83.12 percent of schools having the internet facilities.
But the trend of progress from 2015 to 2022 in every respect were shown significantly.
              Chapter – One
Introduction, objectives and survey methodology
                                     Chapter: One
                    Introduction, objectives and survey methodology
Introduction

Education plays key role in the development of any country. It is world-wide recognized that a
rapid improvement of education is end result for accelerating economic, social and human
development. The overall development can be achieved through proper and well-planned
education system catering to the diverse needs of the nation.

Considering the importance of education in building the nation all the governments in Bangladesh
regardless of their political character, affiliation and ideological learnings appeared to have
assigned a high priority to the expansion of access, equity and quality of education at all levels.
The present government also has taken different steps for the development of the education system
with the firm impression to build digital Bangladesh.

In order to achieve the goal of vision 2021, effective education planning and management are very
much essential. Updated, reliable and accurate data set is indispensable for the coherent
educational planning, development and management of educational system in Bangladesh. The
MOE is responsible for the planning and development of education sector. It is also responsible for
the effective and efficient management of the educational institutions of the country. To this end
the MOE entrusted the BANBEIS with the responsibility of providing valuable and authentic
information. The MOE asked the BANBEIS to follow scientific methods to establish facts and
figures for taking appropriate decisions.

With a view to providing accurate and up-dated data set for planning, development and
management of the education institutions as well as monitoring the progress (changes) of the
sector and sub-sectors, the BANBEIS starting from 2008 regularly conducted a survey of all
educational institutions involved in offering post-primary education. For primary education the
BANBEIS uses the data set regularly collected by the DPE through Annual Primary School
Census.

It is intended to collect through the education surveys all relevant data from all educational
institutions for knowing the parameters of important variables such as access, equity, quality,
continuation, drop-out, transition in relation to student’s participation, teaching and other facility
available in the respective institutions. The target population is enormously large. The number of
variables in each subsector is also big. The tasks involved are therefore gigantic and it not properly
executed, there are changes of non-sampling errors. The BANBEIS has been developing quality
assurance measures to minimize the non-sampling errors.
  The last education Census in the name of National Educational Survey (NES) was conducted in
  2008. Changes are continuously taking place. The number of institutions in each subsector, their
  enrolment, and teachers involved, facility is continuously changing. Many changes took places in
  the education sector. There have been spectacular increases in the number of institutions,
  enrolment and teachers all over the country. It is necessary to know whether equity and quality
  have been and maintained, whether girls are enjoying the fruits of expansion or disadvantaged
  tribes or social groups remain included as before. The existing database needs to be up-dated to
  meet the present day challenged facing the education sector. It is urgently felt the need for
  strengthening database at the BANBEIS. The BANBEIS has been conducting the survey regularly
  since 2008. The surveys 2009-2021 were conducted and the reports up to 2021 were published.
  The present report consisting statistical tables along with analysis in some cases.

  Aims and objectives of educational survey 2022

  The aims of the survey 2022 are;
  a. To collect up to date quality data for 2022 from all post primary education institutions to build
     a strong database and add the information of new institutions and delete the information of
     abolished institutions from the database.
  b. To develop skill of the BANBEIS professional in respect of conducting the surveys,
     monitoring, evaluation and research.
c.    To increase information awareness of teachers and administrators working in education with
      the data collected through the surveys and to simultaneously make both the data providers and
      users aware of the importance of facts and figures.
d.    To impart training to the teachers and administrators working in education for developing skill
      in filling up the questionnaires and also use of facts and figures.

  Specific objectives of the survey 2022

       The specific objectives of the Survey 2022 are;
  I.    To update existing database for post-primary education.
 II.    To publish Bangladesh education statistics 2022.
III.    To increase information awareness among all stake holders (teachers, managers,
        administrator, researchers and other users of information)
IV.     To make all information available to help Policy Makers, Education Managers and Education
        Researchers.
V.      To evolve methodology for assessing the efficiency of educational institution.
   Scope of the educational institution survey 2022.

   All the educational institutions imparting post primary education constitutes the population of this
   Survey. Every institution was the unit of measurement. Every upazila/thana was considered as
   enumeration area. Special attention has been accorded to cover all post-primary education
   institutions.

   Survey Methodology
   Appropriate methods and techniques were employed to conduct the survey. The following
   approaches were followed:

   1. Pre-survey activity
   The following important activities were undertaken to ensure the effective and efficient
   implementation of the survey:
a. In order to know what data were to be collected, BANBEIS conducted consultation
   workshops/seminars/meetings with the users and providers of data and shared their views. After
   getting feedback from workshop questionnaires were finalized;
b. After finalizing questionnaires, a on-line data entry software was developed and uploaded to
   BANBEIS website for data provide;



   2. Questionnaires: Drafting and finalization
   A total of ten questionnaires were developed for survey 2022 In view of the types and levels of
   education the following questionnaires were used for annual education survey 2022.

   (1) Unified Q-1 for school (2) Unified Q-2 for madrasah (3) Unified Q-3 for colleges (4) Unified
   Q-4 for school and colleges (5) Q-5 for Technical and vocational (6) Q-6 for professional
   Education and (7) Q-7 for Teachers Training colleges (8) Q-8 for public Universities (9) Q-9 for
   Private Universities and (10) Q-10 for English medium schools.
   These Questionnaires were sent to relevant offices for their opinions. Their comments were
   incorporated in these Questionnaires. The revised questionnaires were duly pre-tested. The valuable
   comments/observations obtained during pre-tests were considered during finalization of
   Questionnaires.

   3. Data collection, supervision, and monitoring
   BANBEIS has introduced e-survey for online data collection directly from the education
   institutions. After completing data entry and updating by the Institutions, it has been verified by
   the USEOs/assigned officers and submitted data in the central database of BANBEIS. Online data
   collection started on 16 October 2022 and continued up to 5 November 2022. The whole activities
   were supervised and monitored by field officials of BANBEIS and the Ministry of Education.
 4. Data quality control
 BANBEIS took all measures to ensure the quality of data. The following steps were undertaken to
 ensure quality.
    i. Post Enumeration Check (PEC)
    ii. Computerized data cleaning

 4.1 Post Enumeration Check (PEC)
      Post Enumeration Check (PEC) is a statistical practice to measure the extent of error incurred
      in the survey and thus adjust the data collected through 2022 survey. According to survey plan
      BANBEIS conducted post enumeration check to ensure quality and consistency of data. The
      PEC was carried out on a sample basis. The PEC covered school, college and madrasah.
      Detail’s description are shown in the annexure.

 4.2 Computerized data cleaning
      Data cleaning was done by using statistical package software like SPSS and STATA.

5. Data processing
Oracle based database software was developed, in-house with entry, edit and reporting models. The
entry form was developed using Php and Java while oracle 11g was used at the backend. Data
entry was made online directly from the institutions and post entry editing and cleaning was also
made before reporting.

6. Reporting
The initial job was to develop a tabulation plan. This was followed by generation of dummy tables.
The dummy tables formed the basic statement of the report. Finally, the dummy tables were linked
to datasets in the database and the data tables were created. The data tables were then edited to
give the present view. So the reporting flow was as follows:
Tabulation plan      dummy tables database         data tables   statistical tables report.

 7. Limitations

The Annual Education Survey 2022 covers 10 types of institutions located all over Bangladesh.
Record keeping of most institutions was found weak and unsystematic. So, data insert by the Heads
of institution was inadequate in some cases. Some Universities, Medical colleges and English
medium schools did not comply with BANBEIS request. The data for universities were taken from
the annual report 2021 published by BUGC and estimated data of medical and other institutions
were used while preparing this report.

                 Annexure
1. Post Enumeration Check (PEC) Report 2022
           2. Survey Questionnaire
Bangladesh Bureau of Educational Information and Statistics (BANBEIS)
                    Ministry of Education (MoE)




  Post Enumeration Check (PEC) Report 2022




          Statistics Division, BANBEIS, Dhaka, Bangladesh
Introduction
For the effective and efficient management and monitoring the progress of Education sector
BANBEIS regularly conducts an Annual Education Institution Survey (AEIS) of Post-
Primary Education levels. The AEIS collects data from all Post-Primary in 2022 there were
19557 Secondary Schools, 1446 School & Colleges, 3301 Colleges and 9268 Madrasahs.
AEIS data of 2022 gives a total view of Schools and Madrasahs. Among other the AEIS
collects data for knowing the parameters on important variables such as enrolment,
attendance, dropout, pass-rate, teachers, and training facility available at the institution level.
The target population in respect of each variable is enormously big. If data collection is not
properly done, there the chance of non-sampling error increases. These errors effect the
reliability and validity of the estimates. To improve reliability and validity of the survey data
BANBEIS regularly conducts validation sample Survey. The PEC is a standard practice
designed to know the extent of errors present in the AEIS data.
The PEC 2022 was designed to assess primarily the quality of AEIS data in relation to some
important variables such as enrolment, and repetition etc.

1.2. Objectives of 2022 PEC data
     The objectives are:
      To assess the quality of 2022 AEIS data
      To assess the level of accuracy of selected indicators
      To make necessary corrections of data of indicators through correction factor

1.3. Scope of Work
To achieve the objectives of the PEC 2022 it is necessary to collect relevant data through a
nationally representative sample of Schools and Madrasahs. For every sample school collect
data for each variable will be established. This data set will be compared with AEIS data set
to assess the level of accuracy of data set. The validation is expected to identify main factors
for incorrect recording and making AEIS data accurate.

1.4 Sample Size for the PEC 2022
Let n is the sample size for thevalidation sample Survey. We have two sets of data for the
same indicator, say enrolment of a class.
x1c x2c.......xncare n AEIS data x1s, x2s, ..... xns are n PEC data. We take x1s, x2s.........are n
correct data and xic is correct if xic, = xis otherwise xic has error incorrect.
For determining r, the Sample size, we consider the variable enrolment, the most important
variable.
In case the ith institutions is free from error then x1c = x1s
If all Schools are free from errors ∑ (X1c) =∑ (X1s) or

¯x1c=¯x1s, ¯Xc=¯Xs, Where ¯Xs and ¯Xc are population mean
If Pis the percentage of AEIS Schools with no error, Q= 1-P, n= Sample size then the
Standard formula for n is
n= (1.96)2 pq×deff
      d2
≅768 for p=q=0.5, d=0.05 deff = 2
Thus a random Sample of 768 Institutions (Schools, School & Colleges, Colleges and
Madrasahs) would provide estimates at 5% level of significance with 95% confidence level.
1.5 Selection of Schools, School & Colleges, Colleges and Madrasahs
Random Sampling is used to select Sample Schools (428), School & Colleges (60), Colleges
(80), Madrasahs (150) and Technical and Vocational Educational Institutions (50).

Data Analysis, Findings and Conclusions

The AEIS data are available for all school, College and Madrasah. The BANBEIS provided
data for the schools, College and madrasah collected through AEIS 2021. The data set for
sample Schools is: x1c, x2c ….... xnc. The data collected through PEC are; x1s, x2s, ........, xns.
For ith institution the survey observation is xic and the survey observation is xis.
The difference xic-xis is the error for the ith school.
ei=x1c-x1s

(X1c-X1s) is zero for all i-1, 2....N.

   2.7 Conclusion and Recommendation
   For the indicators on enrolment, the relative difference between AEIS average and PEC
   average is found minimum. So, correction to the AEIS data is not required.

   The overall quality of AEIS 2022 data is good and up to the mark. To improve further,
   training of data management at the institution as well as central levels should be given more
   emphasis.

৪.১২.১০ প্রশতষ্ঠানটি প্রশতবছর এবাং েীঘ িদময়ােী দুদ িাগ ঝশুঁ ক সাংক্রান্ত ক্ষকান মূল্যায়ন প্রশতদবেন কদরদছ/পাঠিদয়দছ কী?

         ১          িুাঁ, শবভাগীয় ছক ও শনদে িশনা অনু ায়ী পাঠাদনা িয়                 ২           সমস্যাসমূি সনাক্ত ও তাশলকাভুক্ত করা িদয়দছ


         ৩          ক্ষ াদন প্রশতষ্ঠান প্রিান কর্তিপক্ষদক অবশিত কদরদছন              ৪           ভাদলাভাদব শনদজদের জন্য কদরদছ
